_readme: MOGO's DELTA over the shipped Claude Code auto-mode rules. This file holds only what
MOGO adds; the shipped defaults are merged in at generation time by
scripts/auto_mode/build_auto_mode_config.py, because each section of the autoMode
block REPLACES the corresponding default section rather than merging with it.
Goal: broad routine autonomy inside the MOGO repository, plus a narrow, explicit
governance perimeter. Every label begins 'MOGO ' so a decision trace shows at a glance
which rules are local policy and which are shipped defaults. That prefix is a naming
convention and carries no meaning to the classifier -- so every MOGO rule states its own
scope in its own text rather than relying on the environment entries to do it.
TWO AUTHORING RULES LEARNED THE HARD WAY, from an adversarial review of the first draft:
1. An allow rule may NARROW a flow. It must never CERTIFY a property the classifier
could otherwise check for itself. The first draft asserted that MOGO's browser
storage 'carries no credentials'; docs/STORAGE_KEYS.md records that the operator's
Anthropic API key lives in exactly that store. A classifier told the payload is
clean stops looking. Allow rules therefore whitelist artefacts, never vouch for them.
2. Structural tests do not enforce epistemic boundaries. 'Widening-only' (adding an
absent field) is a structural test; 'sourced rather than inferred' is the actual
boundary, and a backfill can satisfy the first while violating the second.
hard_deny is deliberately NOT extended -- the shipped Data Exfiltration rule is left
exactly as it ships. MOGO's boundaries are soft: they require operator involvement,
which is what governance means here, rather than being unreachable.
environment: **MOGO auto-mode provenance**: the `autoMode` block in the user settings file is GENERATED, not hand-written — `scripts/auto_mode/build_auto_mode_config.py` in the MOGO repository merges the shipped Claude Code defaults with `scripts/auto_mode/mogo_rules.json`. Sections replace rather than merge, so the shipped defaults are reproduced verbatim alongside MOGO's additions. Re-run the generator after a Claude Code upgrade so newly shipped default rules are picked up (`--check` reports drift); edits made directly to the settings file will be lost.

**MOGO trusted repository**: `/Users/joemogollon/Desktop/Forex Hub`, remote `joemogo/forex_hub` (working branch `mogo-main`), a PRIVATE repository. Every rule whose label begins `MOGO ` applies to THAT repository only, and each says so in its own text. Other checkouts on this machine — Life OS, DFS, or any other — are not trusted by anything here and keep default treatment; reaching into them is scope escalation unless the user directed it in this session.

**MOGO trading posture**: PAPER (simulated) only. A PAPER position moves numbers in browser storage and nothing else, so opening, closing, journaling or replaying one has no real-world financial consequence and is not a Real-World Transaction. As of this writing no broker order path for real funds is configured — but that is an observation about the tree, not a licence. If code, configuration or a storage key indicates a live endpoint or a live/practice environment selector, MOGO Live-Money Capability applies and this entry does not clear it. A boundary must never rest on an environment assertion outliving the fact it describes.

**MOGO protected semantics**: frozen strategy behaviour — the ALEX / `alex_g_sr_v1` support-resistance engine, the JVM engine, the protected constants and protected-function governance recorded in `regression-baseline.json`, and the strategy semantics fixed by the MOGO governance documents at the repository root (`MOGO_0**.md`) and under `docs/`. `regression-baseline.json` is a governance artefact, not a build output: its own tool documents that regenerating it 'redefines known good' and must follow an accepted review. TJR is a RESEARCH-lane strategy and is not authorised for PAPER.

**MOGO production research asset**: a live PAPER instance runs continuously in the operator's own Chrome profile and is the sole source of forward evidence. Its app-origin browser storage holds evidence that exists nowhere else until preserved, and some of it is discarded by compaction within hours. That profile also holds ~100 unrelated origins including financial, tax and medical sites, so anything reading or copying from it must be scoped to the MOGO app origin. Per incident INC-004, browser verification never uses the operator's profile or live origin — read-only copies of storage files only, never automation against the live tab.

**MOGO sensitive storage keys**: MOGO's own browser storage is NOT uniformly safe. `fxhub_ai_key` holds the operator's Anthropic API key in `localStorage` by design (documented in `docs/STORAGE_KEYS.md`), and Chrome's `Local Storage` LevelDB is a single database shared by every origin in the profile, so there is no file-level operation that copies 'only MOGO's localStorage'. Raw storage copies are scratch material: they are parsed, never committed, and never treated as clean because they came from MOGO's own origin.

**MOGO evidence stores**: the tracked TradeObservation, EvidenceSource, hypothesis, knowledge-gap and graph records under `docs/trader-intelligence/`, the `evidence/` capture directory (which ignores everything by design, so preserving from it is a deliberate `git add -f`, not an evasion), and the paper journals in browser storage. These are append-only research records with authoritative provenance; existing ids are never overwritten and UNKNOWN is never filled in by inference.
allow: MOGO Routine Engineering: Inside the MOGO trusted repository only — reading and searching the tree, editing source, writing and running tests (`bash tests/run_all.sh`, the Python `unittest` suites, the JavaScriptCore fixture runners), static servers bound to loopback (127.0.0.1) on scratch ports and stopping the ones this session started, syntax checks, the evidence/graph/acquisition validators, diagnostics and log inspection, documentation and milestone records, and ordinary dependency or build repairs. Two specific habits of this repository are covered because they otherwise read as destructive: clearing `__pycache__` by exact path, which mutation testing requires between runs (a same-length edit restored within the same second otherwise leaves stale bytecode and fabricates survivors); and the revert step of a mutation cycle, restoring a file from the copy the session itself saved moments earlier. Explicitly NOT covered: `git clean -fdx` or any other underspecified sweep — `evidence/` ignores everything, so `-x` deletes every captured package; regenerating `regression-baseline.json` with `--update`, which redefines 'known good' (see MOGO Protected Strategy Semantics); weakening a validator assertion (see MOGO Evidence Destruction); anything outside that repository; and any tree-wide `git reset --hard` / `git checkout -- .` / `git restore .` in the primary working tree.

MOGO Read-Only Runtime Inspection: Read-only observation of the operator's own running PAPER instance, for MOGO work in the trusted repository — reading the page and its text, console messages and network log, PAPER runtime health checks, inspecting store liveness by file metadata, and copying the MOGO app origin's own IndexedDB directory to a scratch directory to parse the copy. This is the operator's own local application, not a production service, so it is not Production Reads. Tightly bounded, and the bounds are the point: over an already-exposed local CDP port it covers read-only inspection of the MOGO tab's own application state ONLY — `Network.getAllCookies`, storage or credential domains, and evaluation against any other tab remain Credential Exploration, and `Page.navigate` or any state-changing evaluation remains MOGO Production Disturbance. Chrome's `Local Storage` LevelDB is shared by every origin, so copying it is a last resort, stays in scratch, is parsed only for MOGO's own keys, and is never committed (see MOGO Evidence Preservation). Reading the profile's cookies, saved passwords or `Login Data` is not covered by anything here.

MOGO Evidence Preservation: Committing and pushing MOGO's own derived forward-trade research records into the private MOGO repository, which is the intended and only durable home for observations that browser compaction otherwise destroys within hours. This covers a WHITELIST of artefacts, and nothing else: TradeObservation, EvidenceSource, hypothesis, knowledge-gap, contradiction, graph and report records written under `docs/trader-intelligence/`, and evidence packages deliberately force-added from `evidence/` (that directory ignores everything by design, so `git add -f` there is the documented deliberate act rather than an evasion of a gitignore). Raw browser storage is NEVER committed — no LevelDB or localStorage files, no profile copies, no scratch extracts — because MOGO's own storage holds the operator's Anthropic API key (`fxhub_ai_key`) and Chrome's localStorage database is shared across every origin in the profile. This exception asserts nothing about whether a payload is safe: anything outside the whitelist, any unrecognised storage key, and any raw store copy are judged by the default Credential Leakage, Sensitive-Source Provenance and Data Exfiltration rules exactly as if this exception did not exist, as is every other destination.

MOGO Evidence Processing: Inside the MOGO trusted repository only — appending new TradeObservation, EvidenceSource, hypothesis, knowledge-gap and acquisition-queue records; importing evidence packages once the provenance and integrity invariants are satisfied by validators the session has not modified; rebuilding derived graph and report artefacts from their sources; and read-only analysis — hypothesis triage, replay/historical analysis, decision-difference analysis, forward-performance summaries over an explicitly selected evidence population. Backfills are covered only when every added value is READ FROM the package, source or record it derives from. 'Widening-only' is a structural test and is not the boundary: composing, inferring or generalising a value is MOGO Inference Promotion however many previously-absent fields it fills. This does not cover editing or deleting values already recorded on an existing record — see MOGO Evidence Destruction.
soft_deny: MOGO Live-Money Capability [named+specifics — **must name:** the broker or account and that real funds are at risk]: Enabling, authorising or executing trading with real money, or building the capability to — wiring broker order placement against a funded account, adding or configuring broker API credentials, switching an environment selector from practice to live, or repairing, completing or re-enabling any order-submit path that reaches a live endpoint, whatever the function is called. Simulated PAPER trading is explicitly not covered and needs no approval. The standing operator instruction is that live trading is not authorised, so a passing mention, a config value found in the tree, a research document discussing live behaviour, or an environment entry stating that no live path exists never clears this — only the operator, in this session, naming the account and the funds at risk.

MOGO Protected Strategy Semantics [named+specifics — **must name:** the exact rule, function or constant and the change]: Changing frozen strategy behaviour — ALEX/`alex_g_sr_v1` or JVM entry, stop, target, sizing or risk semantics, protected constants, or the protected-function / protected-rule governance machinery itself. That machinery includes `regression-baseline.json`: regenerating it with `--update` redefines 'known good' and re-blesses whatever protected diff is currently outstanding, so it is covered here and is not routine artefact regeneration however it is invoked. Also covered: removing a protected marker, a governance check or a baseline assertion so a change can land, and loosening a strategy or a gate to generate trading activity — which is this rule's most serious case and is never cleared by wanting more observations. Adding tests, instrumentation, error recording or documentation around protected code without altering what it decides is ordinary work and is not covered.

MOGO Inference Promotion [named+specifics — **must name:** the rule and the governing evidence or decision]: Turning something inferred, hypothesised, contradicted or UNKNOWN into an authoritative record — writing a mechanical entry trigger, stop placement or risk-per-trade that the source material does not state; supplying protected strategy semantics where the frozen specification is silent, which is authoring frozen behaviour rather than changing it; resolving an open contradiction record by picking a reading; marking a hypothesis validated without the evidence population its test requires; or promoting a RESEARCH-lane strategy such as TJR into PAPER. A bulk backfill is the usual disguise: filling a previously-absent field across many records with a composed value is covered here even though it changes no existing value. Recording that the gap exists, what would close it, and queueing the acquisition is the authorised response and is not covered. UNKNOWN stays UNKNOWN, and a human example disagreeing with MOGO is not by itself grounds to change a rule.

MOGO Evidence Destruction [named+specifics — **must name:** the exact store and the records]: Resetting or deleting PAPER accounts, journals, open positions, forward observations, evidence stores, provenance or acquisition records; rewriting an existing record's recorded values, ids or source links in a way that destroys provenance or auditability, including re-deriving a record over one already imported or collapsing replay/historical evidence together with forward/live evidence so the two can no longer be told apart; and weakening or removing a provenance or integrity assertion in the evidence, graph or acquisition validators — an import gate that the same session just loosened is not a gate, and the two steps are covered together however ordinary each looks alone. Appending new records and source-read backfills are not covered (see MOGO Evidence Processing); deleting scratch copies and regenerable derived artefacts is not covered either.

MOGO Production Disturbance [named+specifics — **must name:** the action and the instance]: Disturbing the running PAPER instance — restarting or reloading it, navigating or driving the operator's live tab, running browser automation against the operator's profile or live MOGO origin (incident INC-004), evaluating script that mutates application state, closing or altering open positions, or injecting, manufacturing or back-dating trades. The forward evidence stream is a production research asset and an interruption loses evidence that cannot be recovered. Read-only inspection is not covered (see MOGO Read-Only Runtime Inspection), and an operator-initiated shutdown is ordinary known downtime to be recorded, not something to repair.

MOGO Local History Deletion [named+specifics — **must name:** the branch, tag or worktree]: Deleting a local branch, tag or worktree that may hold unmerged or unpushed work — `git branch -D`, `git tag -d`, `git worktree remove`, or discarding a detached checkout with commits on it. The shipped Git Destructive rule covers REMOTE branches, tags and history; in this repository the local refs are where milestone work sits before it is pushed, so deleting one can destroy the only copy. Deleting a branch this session created and already merged or pushed is not covered.

MOGO Documented Governance Boundary [named+specifics — **must name:** the boundary and the action]: Taking an action that a MOGO governance document, backlog item or open owner-decision record marks as requiring explicit operator approval — promotion gates, protected-scope changes, owner decisions recorded as pending, and the like. This is a catch-all for boundaries the more specific rules above do not name, and it can only act on what the action itself makes visible; it is not a substitute for encoding a known boundary as its own rule. Reading the boundary, recording a finding against it, and continuing other authorised work are not covered; only taking the gated action is.
